multi-source fact extraction evaluator: Do not award separate rule credit for immutable source files used to derive answers; those checks are positive before the task starts and create false positives. The reward should be anchored to the user-created artifact containing the derived facts.
plain-text exact-line verification: For tasks requiring exactly N lines, avoid filtering to non-empty lines; compare the full file content to the expected string with at most one final newline so extra blank lines or partial values cannot pass.
PPTX text box parsing with python-pptx: When inspecting placeholders, do not call hasattr(shape, 'placeholder_format') because python-pptx may raise ValueError for non-placeholder text boxes. Use shape.is_placeholder before accessing shape.placeholder_format, or avoid placeholder_format entirely by collecting slide text.
plain-text exact-line audit files: When the instruction requires exactly one line, avoid using strip() on the whole line because it permits leading/trailing spaces and extra blank trailing lines; compare the raw content against the exact allowed string plus optionally a single final newline.
PPTX title verification: When verifying slide titles, do not rely only on placeholder idx or shape names; WPS users may create titles as ordinary text boxes, so combine placeholder checks with positional/font-size heuristics or accept exact required title text anywhere on the expected slide while separately checking body text.
PPTX content verification: For presentation tasks, parse the saved PPTX and score only the requested output artifact; require exact slide count and exact title text, and distinguish title placeholders from body/text-box content to avoid substring false positives.
PPTX presentation verification: When verifying a multi-subgoal PPTX task, avoid adding redundant full-credit rules for a single subgoal because aggregation can let partial artifacts pass. Prefer one parser rule that enforces slide count, exact titles, and separate body text requirements together.
PPTX structural verification: For presentation tasks, parsing the saved PPTX with python-pptx and checking slide count, title placeholders/top text, and non-title text shapes is a reliable alternative to VLM-only verification.
PPTX slide count and content verificatio: When the instruction requires exactly two slides, the evaluator should assert len(prs.slides) == 2 rather than only checking for at least two slides, and should verify required text on the intended slide/placeholders rather than allowing any extra-slide or body-text match.
PPTX slide content verification: When a task specifies title, subtitle, or text-box placement, python-pptx checks should inspect placeholder types/indices or non-title text frames separately, not just search all slide text.
plain-text exact line count: For tasks requiring exactly N lines, evaluate raw splitlines including blank lines rather than filtering to non-empty lines, otherwise files with extra blank lines can falsely pass.
PPTX exact slide and textbox structure: For presentation tasks requiring exact slide counts or exact textbox lines, parse the PPTX and explicitly reject extra slides, extra non-title text shapes, extra lines, or out-of-order lines; checking only that expected strings appear is too permissive.
PPTX exact text box verification: When an instruction requires an exact text box with specific lines, parse all non-title text shapes and reject extra non-title text rather than awarding most credit for the required strings appearing anywhere.
speaker notes verification: Speaker notes in PPTX should be verified by parsing the notesSlides XML and extracting the actual notes body placeholder text; avoid substring or keyword partial credit when the instruction requires an exact note.
PPTX speaker notes verification: When the instruction requires an exact speaker note, the rule should compare the normalized notes body text exactly and should not award substring credit, because default or extra notes text can otherwise create false positives.
initial-state scoring: Generic existence/validity checks on pre-existing source files should not contribute positive reward by themselves; use them only as gates within content rules or they will cause init_reward_positive failures.
